deep_analysis.executive_intro:
The FTSE screen is broadly neutral-to-selective: 249 names carry actionable signals (20 strong buys, 50 buys) against 134 holds and 44 avoids, so value is concentrated rather than market-wide. Among the five highest-ranked names, two Industrials (FGP.L, MEGP.L) sit alongside single representatives from Healthcare (HIK.L), Communication Services (ITV.L), and Agriculture/Commodities (AEP.L)—a modest Industrials tilt but no single-sector dominance. Several headline strong buys were downgraded to Buy after overlays (FCF basis, earnings basis, interim quality, healthcare pricing), leaving AEP.L as the only name retaining an unadjusted strong_buy. Caution: multiple top picks show material FCF and earnings-definition divergence across filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted figures, and all five are new signals (1 week, low conviction scores)—quantitative passes should not be treated as fully reconciled fundamentals.

FGP.L (FirstGroup plc, Industrials) scored composite 91% (10/22 models, sector-relative 86%), passing all five factor families on cheapness metrics including P/E 9.2, P/B 1.4, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.7%, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality. It failed Graham Defensive/Enterprising, Financial Health (D/E 161%, current ratio 0.73), FCF Yield (basis mismatch: filing $362.6M vs screen TTM $302.8M vs company-adj £113.5M), and quality/moat screens citing thin margins and high leverage; statutory earnings growth is -5.9% despite adjusted EPS growth +16%. With two Industrials in the top five, sector concentration is moderate. Verdict: watchlist — cheap on headline multiples and strong Piotroski, but leverage, liquidity, FCF/earnings basis overlays, and negative statutory growth warrant confirmation before sizing.

MEGP.L (ME Group International, Industrials) ranks second on breadth with 15/22 passes (composite 84%, sector-relative 89%), including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Magic Formula, and Financial Health, on P/E 7.9, P/B 2.3, yield 7.1%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%. Failures include Piotroski F-Score (6/9), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and Lynch PEG (negative earnings growth -3.9%); interim-quality overlay flagged declining interim EPS and FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (gross -0.90×, net 0.84×), adjusting signal to Buy. Industrials pairing with FGP.L adds sector overlap. Verdict: watchlist — exceptional value/quality scores, but dividend sustainability and interim cash conversion need validation before accumulate.

HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals, Healthcare) posts composite 81% (10/22, sector-relative 91%) on Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Financial Health, with P/E 12.5, P/B 1.9, yield 3.9%, ROE 15.4%, D/E 77%. It fails FCF Yield (3.5% vs 5% threshold), Earnings Yield (8.0% at cutoff), Piotroski (6/9), Earnings Quality (weak FCF conversion), and yield screens; healthcare price-erosion, earnings-basis, and FCF-basis overlays all adjusted signal to Buy (filing FCF $119M vs screen TTM $14.4M). No sector cluster risk (sole Healthcare name). Verdict: watchlist — quality-income profile is attractive, but US generic pricing pressure and FCF/earnings definition gaps argue against full conviction until filings reconcile.

ITV.L (ITV plc, Communication Services) delivers 14/22 passes (composite 78%, sector-relative 88%) including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.45, growth 26.7%), High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health, on P/E 11.9, P/B 1.6, yield 7.0%, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%. Failures include Piotroski F-Score (3/9), FCF Yield (basis mismatch: filing $148M vs screen TTM $211.9M vs company-adj £325M), Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat; FCF-basis overlay adjusted to Buy. FCF/dividend coverage net is 0.79×. Sole Communication Services name—no sector cluster. Verdict: watchlist — deep value and income metrics screen well, but structurally weak Piotroski, advertising cyclicality, and wide FCF definition spread require qualitative work before accumulate.

AEP.L (AEP Plantations, Agriculture/Commodities) is the cleanest quantitative profile: 18/22 passes (composite 82%, sector-relative 76%), the only top name retaining unadjusted strong_buy, passing Graham Defensive, Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield (12.0%), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health on P/E 10.7, P/B 1.6, yield 5.4%, ROE 15.1%, D/E 0.09%, current ratio 8.69, FCF/dividend coverage net 2.42×. Only failures: Graham Net-Net (missing NCAV), Schloss/Deep Value (P/B above 1.0), Lynch PEG (PEG 1.43). No sector concentration (sole Agriculture/Commodities). Verdict: accumulate — broad model agreement, fortress balance sheet, and no basis overlays; remaining risk is commodity/cyclical exposure outside the screen's scope.

- FGP.L: High leverage (D/E 161%) and weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73) are not fully captured by value passes; transport/industrial cyclicality and contract-renewal risk are open questions. Pension and governance not in JSON.
- MEGP.L: 7.1% yield with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× and gross coverage -0.90× raises dividend-cut risk; photo-booth/vending exposure to discretionary spend and venue cycles not modeled. Interim EPS decline flagged but root cause unknown.
- HIK.L: Healthcare price-erosion overlay signals US generic pricing pressure; statutory earnings growth -4.7% vs adjusted +1.7% suggests accounting/one-off complexity. FDA/regulatory and pipeline concentration risks not in screen.
- ITV.L: Piotroski 3/9 implies deteriorating fundamentals despite earnings rebound; advertising/media cyclicality and streaming competitive pressure not quantified. 7.0% yield with net FCF coverage 0.79× is a balance-sheet/dividend sustainability concern. Governance and pension deficit: insufficient data in JSON.
- AEP.L: Agriculture/commodity cyclicality (timber/plantations) and weather/regulatory land-use risk not captured; small-cap liquidity and related-party/governance questions not in JSON.

question_outcomes.question: 7.1% yield with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× and gross coverage -0.90× raises dividend-cut risk; photo-booth/vending exposure to discretionary spend and venue cycles not modeled. Interim EPS decline flagged but root cause unknown.
question_outcomes.evidence: The 0.84× net coverage is confirmed on a consistent FY2025 basis: net OCF £90.8m less capex £65.6m = filing-aligned FCF £25.2m vs dividends paid £29.8m (`financials_annual.json`, `filings/bodies/f40be706e75a10ae.txt`). The −0.90× gross coverage is a period-mismatch artefact: H1 FY2026 gross cash generated from operations of £38.7m (`filings/bodies/ac9d0c965a93c3fd.txt`) paired with FY2025 annual capex (£65.6m) and dividends (£29.8m) yields gross FCF of −£26.9m and −0.90× coverage — matching `screening_snapshot.json`. On a consistent FY2025 basis (gross OCF £115.5m − capex £65.6m), gross coverage would be ~1.68×. H1 diluted EPS fell to 6.48p (−3.9%) because PBT declined 3.8% to £32.7m on higher depreciation (£23.5m), absence of a £1.6m H1 2025 property gain, equipment sales −14.2%, Photo.ME −6.2%, and April consumer weakness (Photo.ME −17%, Wash.ME +3% — `filings/bodies/e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt`). Interim DPS cut to 3.60p (−6.5%); >55% PAT policy reiterated. Principal risks flag discretionary-spend sensitivity; laundry described as needs-driven. Forward dividend-cut risk under £69–74m PBT guidance remains unquantified.

Exact mechanical reconciliation of Yahoo's $14.4m TTM to filing quarters is **not possible** from local sources (no quarterly cash-flow series in `financials_annual.json`).

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International operates ~49,000 self-service vending units across 16 countries, led by Photo.ME photobooths and the fast-growing Wash.ME laundry franchise. FY2025 (to 31 October 2025) delivered record profit before tax of £78.2m on £315.4m revenue, with net cash of £26.5m and a 7%+ dividend yield at current screening multiples (P/E 7.9, P/B 2.3). The quantitative screen flags cheapness, quality, dividend and GARP simultaneously—a rare combination for a business with 38% EBITDA margins and 28% ROE. The central debate is whether laundry rollout and capital returns (8.64p DPS, £18m buyback) outweigh near-term earnings pressure from German photo-ID regulation, an April 2026 consumer slowdown, and governance friction around delayed FY2025 accounts and a cash-in-transit restatement. H1 FY2026 profit before tax fell 3.8% and full-year guidance was cut to £69–74m PBT.
documents.investment_thesis: The screen’s Strong Buy signal rests on a structurally cash-generative vending estate with high barriers to entry (long-term site contracts, no customer >2% of turnover), accelerating mix shift into higher-margin laundry (Wash.ME EBITDA +18% in FY2025; 46% of group EBITDA), and a valuation that prices little growth (P/E below 8× against mid-single-digit constant-currency profit growth). Fifteen of twenty-two models pass across five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk—including Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Magic Formula, Buffett Quality and High Dividend Yield. Balance-sheet quality supports the screen: debt/equity ~28%, current ratio 1.5×, positive net cash, and operating cash flow of £115.5m in FY2025 (filing-aligned FCF £25.2m after £65.6m capex). Management is explicitly returning capital (58% payout; £18m buyback launched March 2026) while reinvesting in estate expansion (>1,300 laundry installs targeted in FY2026, ASDA partnership). For a value investor, the hook is a dominant, asset-heavy franchise trading at a high yield and low multiple, with an identifiable growth engine (laundry) partially offsetting mature photobooth cash flows. The screen’s interim-quality overlay (H1 EPS decline; net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84×) appropriately moderates headline conviction—the adjusted signal is Buy, not unqualified Strong Buy.
documents.financial_review:
Primary source: 61 filing bodies in `filings_index.json` (annual, interim, trading update, governance RNS).

**Annual FY2025** (`filings/bodies/f40be706e75a10ae.txt`, `ir_59ec4565fa7e453b.txt`): Revenue £315.4m (+2.4%); PBT £78.2m (+6.5%); EPS 14.91p (+4.5%); EBITDA £120.4m (38.2% margin). Wash.ME +17.3%; Photo.ME −4.0%. Cash generated from operations £115.5m; net cash from operations £90.8m; capex £65.6m; filing-aligned FCF £25.2m (`financials_annual.json`). Dividends £29.8m; DPS 8.64p (58% of EPS). Net cash £26.5m. Net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84×; annual-consistent gross coverage ~1.68×.

**Interim H1 FY2026** (`filings/bodies/ac9d0c965a93c3fd.txt`): Revenue £154.3m (+0.3%); EBITDA £57.0m (+7.1%); PBT £32.7m (−3.8%); EPS 6.48p (−3.9%). PBT bridge: higher depreciation (£23.5m); £1.6m prior-year gain absent; equipment sales −14.2%; Photo.ME −6.2%; April shock (Photo.ME −17%, Wash.ME +3%). OCF £38.7m; capex £33.9m; ~£4.8m H1 FCF vs £14.5m dividends (~0.33×). Interim DPS 3.60p (−6.5%); net cash £7.5m.

**Trading update** (`filings/bodies/e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt`): FY2026 PBT £69–74m; April weakness in France; May recovery +11.1% vending revenue.

The 7.1% yield reflects FY2025 DPS against a price embedding the guidance cut. The −0.90× gross coverage is not an economic signal — it pairs H1 gross OCF with FY capex/dividends. Real dividend pressure exists (net 0.84× FY2025; H1 interim cut) but is mitigated by gross cash £52.8m and management's willingness to trim the interim.

Gaps: no FY2026 final-dividend guidance; FY2022–23 from Yahoo only; screen TTM FCF basis unexplained in filings.
documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced:** FY2025 net FCF under-covered dividends (0.84×); H1 interim DPS cut while buybacks continued (`ac9d0c965a93c3fd.txt`, buyback bodies); gross −0.90× is a scoring period mismatch, not annual cash failure; April consumer slowdown and discretionary-spend risk in principal risks (`e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt`); German ID regulation; audit delay and suspension (`4e623d8eb77b8f49.txt`, `32f4d3a0361630fd.txt`); Concert Party buyback waiver (`050e503ab7d4e46e.txt`); cash-in-transit restatement; net cash £7.5m with going concern affirmed.

**Still open:** forward dividend under £69–74m PBT → IR presentation or H2 update; boardroom press claims → Investors' Chronicle full text; universe screen stats → weekly run manifest.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC (HIK.L) is a diversified generic and specialty pharmaceutical group spanning US injectables, US retail (Hikma Rx), and MENA branded generics, reporting in US dollars. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy (10/22 models; composite 81%; P/E 12.5, P/B 1.9, yield 3.9%, ROE 15.4%), supported by cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk families. Filings show FY2025 core revenue of $3,349m (+6%) and core operating profit of $741m (+3%), with H1 2026 core operating profit up 9% and full-year 2026 guidance reiterated. The valuation hook is a FTSE 100-quality franchise trading below historical multiples after a February 2026 guidance reset, partially recovered on a strong H1 beat and a $250m buyback. The central debate is whether Branded and Hikma Rx momentum can offset Injectables margin erosion, elevated capex and weak reported free cash flow, and whether withdrawn medium-term guidance signals a structural reset rather than a cyclical trough.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination: a globally diversified, investment-grade (BBB/stable, S&P and Fitch) pharmaceutical platform with visible cash returns (84 cents total dividend in FY2025, +5%; $250m 2026 buyback) at modest absolute and sector-relative multiples. The screen passes Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value and Financial Health — a breadth consistent with a quality compounder mispriced on near-term noise rather than balance-sheet distress.

Business quality is underwritten by segment leadership: third-largest US generic injectables supplier by volume and largest MENA pharma company by sales (FY2025 results release). US manufacturing (Ohio, New Jersey) provides a structural advantage amid tariff discussions. Branded delivered 10% core revenue growth and 19% core operating profit growth in FY2025; H1 2026 Branded revenue rose 15% with a 32.5% core margin. Hikma Rx margins improved to 17.3% in FY2025 and 20.6% in H1 2026 on mix and contract manufacturing.

The screen's adjusted signal (strong buy downgraded to buy) flags three reconciliations that a value investor should embrace rather than ignore: (1) healthcare price-erosion overlay — Hikma Rx faces "modest price erosion" per H1 2026 interim; (2) earnings-basis overlay — statutory EPS growth is flat to negative while core EPS grew 2% in FY2025; (3) FCF overlay — filing-aligned FCF of $119m in FY2025 versus screen TTM of $14.4m, with FCF yield failing at 3.5% versus a 5% threshold. These are not disqualifiers for a quality-value entry but define the diligence burden: the margin of safety lies in core earnings power and asset base, not in near-term cash conversion.

Governance has stabilised after disruption: Said Darwazah returned as CEO (December 2025), Victoria Hull became Chair, and a CFO search is under way (Acting CFO: Areb Kurdi). Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly — dividend growth, buyback, and continued R&D (5% of revenue in H1 2026, +18% spend). Net debt/core EBITDA of 1.6x at year-end 2025 and 1.9x at H1 2026 remains manageable within investment-grade headroom.

documents.name: ITV plc
documents.executive_summary:
ITV is a UK-listed media group transitioning from a vertically integrated broadcaster-producer into a global content studio, with the proposed sale of Media & Entertainment (M&E) to Sky representing the defining strategic event. The quantitative screen rates the name a **strong buy** (14/22 models; composite 78%), anchored by low multiples (P/E 11.9, P/B 1.6), a ~7% dividend yield, and resilient adjusted earnings through a difficult linear advertising cycle. The valuation hook is twofold: headline cheapness on earnings and yield, plus a potential **~£950 million** net cash return to shareholders on completion of the Sky transaction (announced July 2026), leaving a listed ITV Studios business. The central debate is whether the market is correctly pricing (a) post-deal residual earnings power and capital returns, (b) UK advertising cyclicality and regulatory clearance risk on the Sky merger, and (c) whether reported free cash flow truly covers the dividend once working-capital swings and deal costs are included.

documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, ITV offers a recognisable Graham/Lynch profile: double-digit earnings yield, sub-3× P/B, a maintained **5.0p** ordinary dividend (~7% yield on screening inputs), and debt/equity of ~52%. The screen passes five metric families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with models including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG, Magic Formula, and Acquirer's Multiple.

Business quality is better than the share-price narrative suggests. Filings show successful execution of the “More Than TV” strategy: **two-thirds of revenue** now from ITV Studios and digital M&E (FY 2025 full-year results, March 2026); ITVX digital advertising up **12%** in FY 2025; ITV Studios external revenue up **10%**. Cost discipline has delivered **£253m** of permanent savings since 2019. Management has returned **>£1.6bn** to shareholders since 2018 via dividends and buybacks.

The screen signal is not unqualified. **FCF Yield** fails because filing-aligned FCF (**£148m** / $148m on the screen) diverges from company-adjusted FCF (**£325m** per screen overlay). Statutory FY 2025 free cash flow in the annual RNS was **£187m**—enough to notionally cover the ~**£190m** dividend but with little headroom. Piotroski F-Score is **3/9** (weak trend quality: leverage not declining, margins not improving). Buffett Quality and Economic Moat fail on ROE (~13.5%) and margin thresholds. The investment case therefore rests on **adjusted earnings resilience + yield + optionality from the Sky deal**, not on pristine cash-conversion trends.

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run screened 249 actionable names (20 strong_buy, 50 buy) with 70 buy-tier tickers, but conviction on the headline top picks remains constrained by systemic data-quality gaps rather than by filing volume alone. Gap-fill on MEGP.L, HIK.L, and ITV.L materially improved memo grades (three “strong” vs mostly “adequate” initial memos elsewhere), yet every gap-fill question stayed only partially_resolved and all five top-ranked names carry 1-week “new” signals with low conviction scores. The dominant blocker is scoring-metadata divergence—FCF and earnings figures disagree across filing-aligned, screen TTM, and company-adjusted bases (e.g. HIK.L filing FCF $119M vs screen TTM $14.4M; FGP.L three-way FCF spread)—which triggered overlay downgrades on four of five top names and leaves AEP.L as the sole unadjusted strong_buy. Filing ingest is broadly healthy for buy-tier coverage (69/70 tickers fully bodied; only TW.L flagged thin), but memo source_counts show most initial memos feeding on ~10–20 filing bodies despite 55–115 indexed filings, so research prompts are under-using available corpus. These weaknesses do not invalidate the screen’s value signals but they do block full-size conviction on FGP.L, MEGP.L, HIK.L, and ITV.L until FCF basis reconciliation and period-aligned coverage metrics ship.
post_run_review.persistent_weaknesses:
- **Ingest — filing body extraction (107 backlog items, largest cluster):** Recurring theme of indexed filings without usable bodies or truncated PDF/OCR extracts. Backlog samples cite AEP.L (31 indexed, 0 bodies), MEGP.L ticker_rns_api (52 indexed, 0 bodies historically), ITV.L Companies House PDFs (five refetches, zero bodies), and CH/RNS deep sections missing (FGP.L truncates at ~p.10; ITV.L IR FCF bridge mid-table). This week’s run partially mitigated MEGP.L (32→61 bodies) and ITV.L (33→63) but the pattern persists elsewhere.

- **Ingest — IR presentation and structured table parse (high-priority recurring):** Multiple tickers request `company_ir_presentation` fetch and cash-bridge/segment table extraction (HIK.L, MEGP.L, ITV.L, FGP.L in recent samples). Without structured FCF, segment margin, and dividend-policy fields, gap-fill cannot close overlay questions.

- **Ingest — Yahoo/quarterly cash-flow gaps:** Repeated suggestion to ingest Yahoo quarterly cash-flow into `financials_annual.json` for mechanical TTM reconciliation (HIK.L $14.4M vs $119M unexplained at quarter level; MEGP.L OCF populated in JSON but `None` in fetch causing false Piotroski failures).

- **Scoring — FCF basis and divergence handling (58 backlog items):** Cross-ticker theme: when `fcf.divergence_flagged` or filing vs screen TTM differ by >25%, models still consume unreliable Yahoo TTM inputs. HIK.L, FGP.L, ITV.L, and MEGP.L all surface this. Related: reconcile conflicting FCF fields within `screening_snapshot.json` (HIK.L `key_metrics.FCF` −$66.1M vs `cashflow_metrics.free_cashflow` +$119M).

- **Scoring — period-mismatched coverage ratios:** MEGP.L gross FCF/dividend coverage −0.90× is an artefact of pairing H1 gross OCF with FY capex/dividends; annual-consistent gross ~1.68×. Prompt/scoring both lack explicit gross-vs-net period alignment when `interim_quality_overlay` fires.

- **Scoring — sector overlays and classification:** Healthcare price-erosion overlay (HIK.L), media TAR cyclicality (ITV.L), agriculture sector mapping (AEP.L), and Piotroski/FCF caps for healthcare appear repeatedly across backlog and this_run_suggestions.

- **Prompt — gap-fill output rigour (31 backlog items):** Require explicit period reconciliation for coverage metrics, flag misattributed bodies as ingest failures (HIK.L trading-update URL carrying interim duplicate), and mandate pension/governance extracts before accepting “insufficient data” verdicts (ITV.L).

- **Ops/coverage — universe-level metadata:** Attach weekly FTSE350 run manifest to ticker gap-fill packs so universe counts (249 actionable, overlay downgrade counts) are verifiable locally rather than asserted from deep-analysis prose.

Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.

Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.

question_outcomes.question: Healthcare price-erosion overlay signals US generic pricing pressure; statutory earnings growth −4.7% vs adjusted +1.7% suggests accounting/one-off complexity. FDA/regulatory and pipeline concentration risks not in screen.
question_outcomes.evidence: Expanded body corpus (58 extracts per `filings_index.json`) confirms pricing language at multiple intensities: CH 2023 cites "low double-digit price erosion" in US Generics (`ch_05557934_MzM4MDgyMzIxMmFkaXF6a2N4.txt`); H1 2026 interim states Hikma Rx faces "modest price erosion across the portfolio, in line with recent history" (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`); IR presentation flags "Increased competition on higher margin products" (`ir_a70365d580129295.txt`). Statutory/adjusted divergence is now mapped to named items in H1 2026 Note 5: H1 2025 comparator included $72m legal settlement, $71m contingent-consideration remeasurement income, and $44m intangible amortisation — H1 2026 reported basic EPS 103 cents (−5%) vs core 128 cents (+5%) on the same half (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`); FY2025 filing shows statutory basic EPS +12% (182 cents) vs core +2% (228 cents) (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`). Screen inputs (−4.7% statutory, +1.7% adjusted, `screening_snapshot.json`) reflect TTM Yahoo net-income trend, not FY filing deterioration. H1 2026 interim embeds the full principal-risk register including Market dynamics (pricing/reimbursement), Product pipeline, Legal/regulatory/IP, and Product quality and safety (cGMP) (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`); 48 submissions and 43 launches in H1 2026 indicate a broad, not single-asset, pipeline. Annual report pages 84–88 remain indexed but not fully extracted in `ir_3a67962eb8770824.txt`.
question_outcomes.next_sources: FDA inspection database (483s/warning letters by Hikma US site); annual report principal-risk pages 84–88 full OCR; revenue concentration by top five products from annual report segment notes

question_outcomes.question: Is US generic price erosion transient or structural, and why does screen TTM FCF ($14.4M) diverge so sharply from filing FCF ($119M)?
question_outcomes.evidence: Filings frame US generic pricing as **structural but moderating in intensity**: CH 2022 "accelerating price erosion" (`ch_05557934_MzMzNzcwNjQxNGFkaXF6a2N4.txt`) → CH 2023 "low double-digit" (`ch_05557934_MzM4MDgyMzIxMmFkaXF6a2N4.txt`) → H1 2026 "modest… in line with recent history" for Hikma Rx (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`). Injectables margin compression (35.3% FY2024 → 27.6% H1 2026) reflects mix, competition on higher-margin products, and planned S&M/R&D investment as much as headline deflation; FY2026 guide 27%–28% (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`, `94eb1f8d38a51fa6.txt`). **FCF divergence is reconciled as a data-basis issue:** filing-aligned FY2025 FCF = OCF $436m − capex $317m = **$119m** (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`, `screening_snapshot.json` `fcf.filing_aligned`); screen TTM **$14.4m** is preserved Yahoo trailing FCF (`fcf.screen_ttm`), flagged by `fcf_basis_overlay`. H1 2026 interim cash-flow statement adds bridge detail: OCF $214m (+33%), investing outflow $150m (PPE $122m, intangibles $31m), working-capital days 264 (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`) — cash generation is recovering, not collapsing. Exact mechanical reconciliation of Yahoo's $14.4m TTM to filing quarters is **not possible** from local sources (no quarterly cash-flow series in `financials_annual.json`).
question_outcomes.next_sources: Yahoo quarterly cash-flow ingest to validate TTM construction; company IR cash-flow bridge slide (`ir_a70365d580129295.txt` partial history only); H2 2025 cash-flow lines from annual report notes

question_outcomes.question: 7.1% yield with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× and gross coverage -0.90× raises dividend-cut risk; photo-booth/vending exposure to discretionary spend and venue cycles not modeled. Interim EPS decline flagged but root cause unknown.
question_outcomes.evidence: The 0.84× net coverage is confirmed on a consistent FY2025 basis: net OCF £90.8m less capex £65.6m = filing-aligned FCF £25.2m vs dividends paid £29.8m (`financials_annual.json`, `filings/bodies/f40be706e75a10ae.txt`). The −0.90× gross coverage is a period-mismatch artefact: H1 FY2026 gross cash generated from operations of £38.7m (`filings/bodies/ac9d0c965a93c3fd.txt`) paired with FY2025 annual capex (£65.6m) and dividends (£29.8m) yields gross FCF of −£26.9m and −0.90× coverage — matching `screening_snapshot.json`. On a consistent FY2025 basis (gross OCF £115.5m − capex £65.6m), gross coverage would be ~1.68×. H1 diluted EPS fell to 6.48p (−3.9%) because PBT declined 3.8% to £32.7m on higher depreciation (£23.5m), absence of a £1.6m H1 2025 property gain, equipment sales −14.2%, Photo.ME −6.2%, and April consumer weakness (Photo.ME −17%, Wash.ME +3% — `filings/bodies/e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt`). Interim DPS cut to 3.60p (−6.5%); >55% PAT policy reiterated. Principal risks flag discretionary-spend sensitivity; laundry described as needs-driven. Forward dividend-cut risk under £69–74m PBT guidance remains unquantified.
